**Visual analysis:**

- **Plant part**: Single tomato leaf (elongated, serrated margin, characteristic shape)
- **Lesion characteristics**: Numerous very small (1-3mm), reddish-brown to dark brown spots scattered across the entire leaf surface
- **Leaf background**: Remains mostly dark green — no yellowing, no large necrotic zones, no powdery coating
- **Pattern**: Spots are discrete, tiny, randomly distributed — not coalescing, no obvious concentric rings, no clear tan/white centers

**Differential reasoning:**

| Disease | Match? |
|---|---|
| **Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato** | Strong — tiny (1-2mm) dark necrotic specks scattered on green leaf, classic presentation |
| Septoria_Leaf_Blotch | Possible — but Septoria spots are usually larger (3-5mm) with tan centers and dark margins; not what I see here |
| Early_Blight | No — requires larger lesions with concentric "target" rings |
| Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus | No — would show bronzing, ring patterns, mosaic |
| Powdery_Mildew | No — no white powdery coating |
| Late_Blight | No — no water-soaked oily lesions or white sporulation |

The tiny, dark reddish-brown specks uniformly scattered on a still-green tomato leaf with no other symptoms is the hallmark presentation of **Bacterial Speck** (*Pseudomonas syringae* pv. *tomato*).
